implementation_notes:
# Shared radix-4 divider for the bench core

DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU share a restoring divider. EX captures the forwarded operands and opcode at launch. Setup forms the operand magnitudes and the 34-bit multiples D, 2D and 3D. Each of four registered rounds runs four radix-4 steps. Each step uses the borrow bits from three parallel 35-bit differences to select the restored remainder and the next two quotient bits. The completed operation selects and sign-corrects the result for EX/MEM on the following cycle, adding six EX cycles.

The divider holds fetch and ID/EX while EX/MEM receives side-effect-free bubbles. An older blocked data access takes priority over launch and acceptance. The completed result and original forwarded operands stay available until EX/MEM accepts them. RVFI reports those captured operands on channel 0. The four `RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` substitutions share the same control sequence and handshake.

The datapath reuses one shift register for the unconsumed dividend and accumulated quotient. For a zero divisor the recurrence produces an all-ones quotient and the dividend magnitude as remainder. The sign logic preserves the all-ones quotient and restores the original dividend for REM. Signed `INT_MIN / -1` yields the required 32-bit quotient pattern and zero remainder through the recurrence. A guarded declaration include lets the requested alphabetical Verilator glob resolve the pipeline types.

## Local verification

- Verilator lint passed in hardware and ALTOPS modes.
- All six cocotb suites passed. The divider suite covers the original arithmetic vectors, 512 additional deterministic operand cases, fixed latency, held completion, reset and consecutive launches. The pipeline suite checks launch priority after an older data stall, immediate consumers, consecutive divides and ordered single retirement with the captured RVFI operands.
- `formal/run_all.sh` passed on the first attempt with 53 checks and zero failures, including all four DIV/REM instruction checks.
- Cosim passed on selftest and all three random traces with and without both stall streams. Stalled CoreMark passed the canonical CRC and validation-string checks.
- Gowin placements measured 39.625, 39.190 and 39.190 MHz for a median of **39.190 MHz**, up from the 5.442 MHz baseline. The marker window measured **4,491,485 cycles** for 10 iterations, matching the baseline. Fitness was **87.25 iterations/s**.

The divider round remains the limiting path in the placement-0 report at 30.531 ns and 127 cells. It runs from one divider remainder register to another.
lesson: - 2026-11-22 hyp-20261122-001-r1s0 (regression, +619.88%): Replacing combinational DIV/REM on the shared EX path with registered radix-4 rounds raised median Fmax from 5.442 to 39.190 MHz, with four cascaded steps per round setting the new timing limit and CoreMark's divide-free marker window staying at 4,491,485 cycles.

title: Share a multicycle divider across RV32M divide and remainder
motivation:
The bench baseline runs at 5.442 MHz. Its 199.837 ns worst path spans
forwarding and the execute ALU before reaching the data-memory path.
The signed and unsigned division and remainder operators are the likeliest
source of that depth. Their combinational results share the execute result
mux with ordinary ALU operations and memory addresses. Moving division to
a registered unit should shorten the clock period for every instruction.
The baseline Verilator trace with both bus stall flags retired two DIVU
instructions in the full CoreMark run and zero DIV/REM instructions in
the 4,491,485 marker-bracketed cycles, so the timed loop has no direct
divide latency cost.

implementation_notes:
# Shared multicycle divider

`DIV`, `DIVU`, `REM`, and `REMU` now share a blocking unit. It registers the unsigned operand magnitudes and `3D` on launch, then advances the 36-bit dividend and quotient shift register and the remainder through three radix-4 digits per cycle for six cycles. Each digit uses three parallel 35-bit trial subtractions. Sign correction uses the held final state. The divisor-zero result falls out of the datapath because zero makes every trial fit. Quotient sign correction is disabled for divisor zero, and remainder sign correction reconstructs the original dividend. The 32-bit result also preserves the defined signed overflow behavior. `RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` latches the existing substitute result at launch and uses the same phase counter and acceptance handshake.

EX captures both forwarded operands for RVFI at launch. Fetch and ID/EX hold while EX/MEM receives bubbles and older instructions drain. Data-memory backpressure takes priority over launch and acceptance. On acceptance, EX/MEM receives the completed instruction and the following instruction can enter EX and use the normal bypass. The top-level interface follows `core.yaml` with single-channel RVFI. A guarded declaration include in `alu.sv` also supports the requested wildcard lint order.

## Verification

- Both normal and ALTOPS Verilator lint passed.
- `bash formal/run_all.sh` passed on the first run with **53 checks passed, 0 failed**, including channel-0 liveness, unique order, and all four divide and remainder instruction checks.
- All six cocotb runners passed. Divider coverage includes the original vectors, 512 seeded random cases, fixed latency, reset while active or pending, and output stability under delayed acceptance. Pipeline coverage includes an older stalled store, a dependent consumer, back-to-back dependent divides, and nine-cycle retirement gaps after a load-use bubble and a redirect with ready buses.
- Co-simulation passed selftest RVFI comparison with ready and randomly stalled buses. CoreMark passed the canonical CRC and marker checks with `--istall --dstall`.

The fast formal suite uses ALTOPS. Real divider arithmetic was exercised by cocotb and co-simulation. The blocking schedule adds seven cycles between adjacent retirements when the younger instruction is a divide and the buses are ready.

## Gowin and CoreMark

| Metric | Baseline | Shared divider |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median Gowin Fmax | 5.442 MHz | 45.134 MHz |
| Worst reported setup path arrival | 199.837 ns | 29.073 ns |
| Marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles | 4,491,485 | 4,491,485 |
| CoreMark fitness | 12.12 iter/s | 100.49 iter/s |

Placement options 0, 1, and 2 reported 42.055, 45.134, and 45.134 MHz. The worst reported setup path was in option 0, from `cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s0` through ID and the execute ALU to `dmem_2_dmem_2_0_0_s` in 15 logic cells. Options 1 and 2 reported a 27.450 ns worst arrival on the redirect feedback path to ID/EX. Gowin reported 3,009 logic cells and 598 registers for option 0, compared with 12,312 cells and 460 registers in the baseline.

Measured fitness increased by **729.1%**, exceeding the 4.6% requirement. Both measurements used ten iterations and the same marker-bracketed cycle count.
lesson: - 2026-11-22 hyp-20261122-002-r1s1 (improvement, +729.13%): Reducing the shared divider from four cascaded radix-4 steps per cycle to three moved the critical path out of the divider and raised median Gowin Fmax from 39.190 to 45.134 MHz, with a nine-cycle retirement gap after a redirect or load-use bubble on ready buses still within the ten-cycle liveness bound.

title: 16-entry tagged branch target buffer
motivation:
The bench core fetches sequentially and discards one fetch slot whenever
EX redirects a taken branch or jump. There is no IF/ID register, so a
correct fetch-stage prediction can remove that entire bubble. The baseline
timing report puts the longest path through the ALU. The predictor can
improve cycles per iteration while keeping its lookup local to fetch.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 16-entry direct-mapped branch target buffer indexed by fetch PC[5:2].
Use PC[19:6] as the tag, target[19:2] as the stored word address, a valid
bit and a two-bit saturating counter. On a word-aligned fetch within the
1 MiB instruction aperture, predict the cached target on a valid tag hit
with the counter's high bit set. Default to PC+4. Train conditional
branches toward their resolved direction, initializing on replacement to
weakly taken or weakly not taken according to the observed outcome. Train
JAL and JALR as strongly taken and refresh the resolved target. Allocate
only legal controls with aligned, in-aperture source and target addresses.
Store the candidate direct target even on a not-taken branch. Read the
target array only at the fetch index, and read tags and counters at both
the fetch and training indices. Reset only the valid bits so the payload
can infer distributed RAM.

Update the fetch PC from the predictor only when IF can enter ID/EX.
The registered fetch PC is then the successor selected for the instruction
in EX and stays paired with it through a dmem hold. For every valid EX
instruction that advances, including non-control instructions, compare its
full resolved next PC with that fetch PC. On a mismatch, give EX recovery
priority over an imem stall and squash the younger instruction before it
enters ID/EX. Train only on advancing EX instructions. Use the same
resolved next PC for recovery and RVFI, including the existing sequential
next PC on misalignment traps.

A scratch prototype running canonical CoreMark with both standard bus
stalls reduced marker-bracketed cycles from 4,491,485 to 4,234,052 and
passed all CRC checks. Gowin measured 5.597 MHz median Fmax across the
three placement options, putting this prototype at 13.22 iterations/s,
about 9.1% above baseline. Recheck both metrics on the tournament build
because placement can move the baseline ALU path. Verify direction
reversals, tag conflicts, changing JALR targets, and recovery during
imem and dmem stalls.

implementation_notes:
# 16-entry tagged branch target buffer

## Implementation

IF indexes the BTB with `PC[5:2]`. An aligned fetch in the 1 MiB aperture uses the cached word target when the entry is valid, the `PC[19:6]` tag matches, and the direction counter is at least 2. The target array has one fetch read port. The tags and counters also have a training read port. Reset clears only the valid bits.

EX trains on advancement. Eligible conditional branches store their direct target for either outcome and saturate their direction counter, starting at the corresponding weak state on replacement. Eligible JAL and JALR write a strongly taken entry with the resolved target. Training requires a legal control instruction and aligned source and target addresses within the instruction aperture.

The registered fetch PC holds the selected successor of the instruction in EX. EX compares the full resolved next PC against that register on every valid advance and uses the same address for RVFI. A mismatch squashes the younger instruction and overrides imem backpressure. The hazard unit generates the EX hold independently of fetch hazards so dmem backpressure defers both recovery and training. Misalignment traps resolve to the existing sequential successor.

The top-level source includes the shared type declarations conditionally so the requested glob-order lint command works alongside the package-first build flows.

## Local verification

- Verilator lint passed with both the requested glob and `make lint TARGET=bench`.
- `bash formal/run_all.sh` passed all 53 single-issue checks with zero failures using the original runner, wrapper, and check configuration staged under `$TMPDIR`.
- `make test TARGET=bench` passed all 83 cocotb cases. Directed pipeline tests check direction reversals and saturation, one training update through a dmem hold, conflicting tags, changing JALR targets, recovery with both bus stalls, and stale predictions on a non-control instruction and a misaligned jump.
- `make cosim TARGET=bench` passed all five ELFs. Selftest and the three random traces passed with both ready modes. CoreMark passed the canonical CRC and validation checks under imem and dmem stalls.

## Tournament build measurements

| Metric | Recorded baseline | BTB |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| CoreMark bracketed cycles for 10 iterations | 4,491,485 | 4,234,052 |
| Gowin median Fmax | 5.442 MHz | 5.334 MHz |
| CoreMark iterations per second | 12.12 | 12.60 |

Gowin reported 4.908, 5.334, and 5.334 MHz for placement options 0, 1, and 2. Option 0 used 12,665 logic cells, 509 registers, and 21 LUT-RAM cells. The longest setup path still crosses the EX ALU, and the lower median Fmax offsets part of the 5.73% cycle reduction. The measured throughput gain is 3.97%.
lesson: - 2026-11-22 hyp-20261122-003-r1s2 (regression, +3.96%): A fetch-local 16-entry tagged BTB saved 5.73% of CoreMark cycles by avoiding redirect bubbles on correct predictions, with the EX ALU still on the critical path and a drop in median post-placement Fmax from 5.442 to 5.334 MHz limiting the throughput gain.

implementation_notes:
# Valid-only fetch and decode bubbles

Fetch passes the raw instruction word to decode. Instruction-memory readiness and EX redirects control fetched validity. The PC keeps redirect priority over all four stall causes and computes the sequential PC directly as `pc + 4`.

ID/EX advances its payload on every edge outside a data-memory or divider hold. Its valid bit clears on reset, holds during either stall, and otherwise takes fetched validity with the load-use interlock applied. The interlock requires a valid load in EX and a ready fetch.

EX qualifies redirects with ID/EX validity and clears register-write, load, and store controls as invalid entries advance into EX/MEM. The existing divider validity guard already covers launch, wait, and acceptance. The existing MEM/WB hold preserves forwarding data while clearing retirement validity during data-memory backpressure.

The directed pipeline test supplies side-effecting words during instruction-memory stalls and at squashed addresses. It checks memory requests, forwarded register values, redirect and divider timing, and channel-0 retirement order. It also exercises a branch that needs MEM/WB forwarding throughout a stalled store.

## Local verification

- Verilator lint passed without warnings.
- All 53 single-channel ALTOPS formal checks passed on the first attempt using `formal/run_all.sh` in a scratch copy of the harness.
- All six cocotb suites passed, including the directed invalid-payload test.
- Co-simulation passed for selftest and all three random traces, both with and without stalls. Stalled CoreMark validated all CRCs and completed 10 iterations in 4,491,485 marker-window cycles.
- `make fpga TARGET=bench NRET=1` measured 45.740, 47.560, and 47.560 MHz. The 47.560 MHz median gives 105.89 CoreMark iterations/s and clears the 47.211 MHz acceptance threshold by 0.349 MHz.

The measured median is 1.035 MHz below the scratch prototype. The longest setup path in each placement reaches data memory through EX.
lesson: - 2026-11-22 hyp-20261122-001-r2s0 (regression, +5.37%): Using valid-only fetch and decode bubbles removes the fetch NOP mux and ID/EX payload clear from redirect feedback, shifting the Gowin timing limit to the EX-to-dmem path and raising median Fmax from 45.134 to 47.560 MHz at the same CoreMark cycle count.

# Retiming bypass selection across the decode-to-execute boundary

Decode compares both source tags against the current ID/EX and EX/MEM destinations. ID/EX captures the four nonzero-destination match bits with the consumer's operands. EX qualifies the matches with the producer's write eligibility and uses a one-hot masked mux for each operand. The younger eligible producer takes priority. The regfile's existing write-first bypass supplies writes already in WB when the consumer issues.

Fetch supplies the raw instruction and uses imem readiness for candidate validity. A redirect from advancing EX updates the PC even during imem backpressure. Redirects and load-use bubbles clear ID/EX validity while the stage captures the payload. A pending older data request or divide wait holds the consumer and its matches. MEM/WB retains forwarding eligibility and data during a data stall while clearing retirement validity. DIV/REM captures the forwarded operands at launch and retains the existing execution schedule.

`forward_unit` handles ID tag matching. EX owns one-hot selection, and the load-use interlock reuses ID's comparisons against the current EX destination. MEM derives backpressure from the valid, aligned bus request, so a misaligned access can retire as a trap while dmem is stalled. The channel-0 RVFI interface follows `nret: 1` in `core.yaml`.

Directed cocotb checks cover matching writers for both operands, a trapping younger writer, the exact load-use bubble, forwarding a retired load across a stalled store, and redirects with both instruction and data backpressure. They check RVFI order and bus writes.

title: Fetch-time direct targets with a 64-entry gshare predictor
motivation:
The current bench champion loses a fetch slot on each taken control
transfer. The previous 16-entry tagged BTB saved 5.73% of CoreMark cycles,
but its Fmax loss left a 3.96% fitness gain. In the champion's canonical
CoreMark trace, conditional branches and JAL account for 96% of taken
transfers. Their targets are available from the fetched instruction. A
small direction table can capture most of the benefit while reducing EX
recovery for direct transfers to a direction check.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
In IF, predecode legal conditional branches and JAL from the fetched
instruction. Compute the full RV32 PC-relative target with a word-address
adder and retain the immediate's bit 1 for alignment checks. Predict an
aligned in-aperture JAL taken and use a 64-entry gshare table for legal
conditional branches with aligned in-aperture targets. Fetch PC+4 for all
other cases, including JALR. Index the two-bit saturating counters by
PC[7:2] XOR the zero-extended two-bit history of resolved conditional
outcomes. Reset history to zero and counters to weakly not taken.

Latch the computed direct target, applied taken bit and lookup index into
ID/EX with the accepted instruction. Advance fetch on that same edge and
keep the existing load-use, divide and dmem hold priorities. EX uses the
latched target for both direct transfers and computes JALR from forwarded
rs1 and the immediate with bit 0 cleared. With the direct target shared
by fetch and EX, a valid advancing instruction only needs a direction
comparison to decide recovery. Squash the younger fetch on a mismatch
by clearing ID/EX at the edge, and set the PC to the true successor even
if imem is stalled. Drive IF's instruction-to-NOP mux only from imem
backpressure so the EX redirect reaches the ID/EX squash directly, off
the instruction, regfile and load-use data paths. Derive the dmem hold
independently of recovery and defer EX recovery while held. Apply the
existing sequential successor, trap, and link-write suppression rules on
misalignment. RVFI always reports the resolved successor.

into the nonspeculative history and queue the latched index and outcome
for a saturating counter update on the following clock. A blocked or
squashed instruction produces no training event. Consecutive updates to
the same entry use the counter updated by the previous event.

implementation_notes:
# Bench gshare predictor

IF predecodes legal conditional branches and JAL, computes their full RV32 direct targets with a 30-bit word-address adder, and carries immediate bit 1 separately for alignment. ID/EX captures the target, applied direction, and six-bit lookup index. For aligned targets within the 1 MiB instruction aperture, fetch predicts JAL taken and uses a 64-entry table of two-bit saturating counters for conditional branches.

EX resolves direct transfers from the latched target and computes JALR from forwarded rs1 and the immediate. The resolved direction drives recovery, and the resolved successor feeds RVFI. A data-memory hold defers recovery and training. When EX advances, a redirect squashes ID/EX and takes priority over instruction-memory backpressure.

Each advancing, opcode-legal conditional branch shifts its comparison outcome into the two-bit history, including when a taken misaligned target traps. A queued update uses the latched lookup index and reads the current counter on the following clock so consecutive updates to an alias accumulate.

I flattened the EX result mux into mutually exclusive ALU, divide, and link result paths after the initial Gowin median measured 43.967 MHz. The final critical paths still run through the EX ALU to the EX/MEM register or dmem RAM. The final build used 3,416 logic cells and 765 registers.

# Two-entry fetch queue

# Bench gshare frontend

Fetch runs ahead through a four-entry flow-through FIFO. The FIFO uses a packed payload array with an asynchronous head read and a synchronous tail write. Each 73-bit entry stores the instruction, 18 source word-address bits, 20 direct-target bits, the applied direction, and two gshare index bits. Decode reconstructs the target alignment bit and the remaining index bits from the packet. The empty bypass carries the full-width source PC and target.

Wrap-bit pointers determine whether the tail slot can be written. A ready response advances the logical tail only when it enqueues, and decode can pop a queued response during an imem stall. For timing, the interlock matches the queue head and raw imem operands in parallel. The bypass acceptance signal therefore reaches fetch without passing through the queue payload mux. Full-width fetch address arithmetic retains 32-bit wraparound semantics.

EX supplies an alternate word address and advancing miss and resume signals. Fetch registers all three and can bypass a ready recovery response to decode in the next cycle. Recovery invalidates queued packets and the younger EX slot, including its forwarding, hazard, memory, divide, and training enables. A blocked recovery request retains its full address for retry. Last-word sequential predictions wait for EX before selecting the aperture successor. RVFI uses the EX-resolved successor and preserves the alignment trap and link-write behavior. Each advancing legal branch trains once using its saved index, including a taken branch that traps on alignment.

The banked register file, one-hot forwarding, split data address path, and nine-edge divider schedule are preserved. The measured worst paths run through the divider and ALU. The queue increases total logic and LUT-RAM use, and placement option 0 alone falls below the frequency needed to clear the throughput hurdle.

- Verilator `-Wall` lint and all 104 cocotb cases passed. Directed tests cover FIFO wraparound, overlapping stalls, recovery retry, wrong-path side effects, both aperture boundaries, queued alignment traps, and exactly-once saved-index training. The existing divider gap and RVFI order checks remain in place.
- `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` passed four full RVFI program comparisons with and without bus stalls, plus the canonical stalled CoreMark CRC check.
- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash formal/run_all.sh` passed all 53 single-issue ALTOPS checks. Formal and co-simulation ran from scratch copies to keep generated files out of the protected directories and shared formal checkout.
- `NRET=1 make fpga TARGET=bench` measured 211.54 CoreMark iterations/s over 3,979,945 marker cycles, a 4.93% gain over 201.60 iterations/s. The three Gowin placements reached 76.603, 84.192, and 84.192 MHz. Placement option 0 used 4,174 logic cells, 950 registers, and 51 LUT-RAM cells, 19 more LUT-RAM cells than the champion.

motivation:

# Shared divider trials

gain. Its replay stream also stops at each branch until imem is ready.

target candidates keeps replay out of the live target calculation.

can enter the issue FIFO. Read from the registered sequential and

# Registered loop replay

Fetch captures taken conditional branch observations from EX or MEM, with MEM supplying the older observation when both stages resolve on the same cycle. The observation is checked for aligned endpoints in the 1 MiB aperture and a backward span of up to 64 words, including both endpoints. The interval governs fills. Resident entries keep their exact tags when a different interval is trained.

The two parity banks register their current and successor matches from the selected registered request. A hold or sequential advance can use a staged match during an imem stall. Taken predictions and recoveries discard the preceding matches and start a lookup at the new request. Replay stores raw instructions, a narrow target, and branch/JAL classification bits. It uses the current gshare lookup and enqueues at the tail of the four-entry logical FIFO. Ready fetch retains its empty-queue bypass. Eight physical slots permit a tentative tail write each cycle.

Live and replay targets have independent registered request candidates. The live packet carries the low target, alignment bit, carry, and displacement sign. EX reconstructs the wrapped upper target for recovery and RVFI. The last-word comparator uses a displacement-based range test to keep the low target adder off the aperture-hold path. FENCE.I invalidates the banks and staged fills at acceptance. A pending-fence count gates replay, loop training, and fills, while the ordinary gshare predictor continues to train from resolved branches. Recovery clears squashed fences and accounts for a fence accepted at the corrected PC.

# Load and store address generation

ID registers the existing one-hot rs1 forwarding decision for decoded loads and stores, plus a displacement-only select for x0. EX computes the three candidate low sums in parallel with the ordinary operand mux, selects the corrected byte address bits [12:0], and checks alignment. EX/MEM also captures the selected raw upper base, the carry-or-borrow condition, and one propagation bit for each upper address bit. MEM applies the upper XOR correction and uses the reconstructed address for both the data bus and aligned RVFI. The EX/MEM hold covers every address component during a data-bus stall.

The selected implementation adds dedicated copies of bits [12:0] of the EX/MEM and MEM/WB forwarding results. Gowin preserves these flops to reduce the load that the low address adders place on the shared forwarding nets. The copies use the same reset and hold conditions as their source results. The displacement sign is included in each 13-bit sum, so the selected bit 12 XOR raw bit 12 gives the same adjustment as the selected low carry XOR displacement sign. The version wired directly to the shared forwarding registers measured 86.886 MHz with the same address arithmetic.

## Verification

- Verilator lint, 116 cocotb cases, and `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` passed. ISS cosim covered selftest and all three random ELFs on ready and stalled buses. The pipeline tests check forwarding priority, x0, carry and borrow, full-width wrap, MMIO, byte lanes, held requests, load-use timing, alignment traps, and wrong-path store suppression.
- A focused, bounded Yosys SAT check compared the EX and MEM address lane with full-width addition of a sign-extended displacement. It passed for all base selections, base values, displacements, alignments, and symbolic stalls and recovery, including bus qualification and the aligned RVFI address and masks.
- Canonical stalled CoreMark validated all CRCs and completed ten iterations in 3,868,036 marker cycles. There were no out-of-bounds accesses.
- The stock single-channel ALTOPS formal run on the final RTL hit the 14-minute local timeout. It generated 53 checks and passed five by the cutoff: retirement cover, liveness, uniqueness, causality, and backward PC. The other 48 checks remain unverified. The logs show solver waits and no counterexample, so no formal repair retries were made.

| 1 | 90.676 | 4 | EX/MEM result through forwarding and the ALU back to EX/MEM result |

on every accepted live word, including an empty bypass, so the RAM
retains the most recent 16 decoded packets. Track the preceding 15
accepted sequential words with a saturating bitmap shifted on live
acceptance. Clear it at a taken prediction, recovery or FENCE.I.
Qualify a legal conditional backedge when the existing gshare predicts
taken, its aligned source and target are within the fetch aperture, and
its negative displacement points to a slot marked by the bitmap. Use
the four low word-offset bits to index the bitmap and to calculate the
loop head as a modular offset from the tail slot being written. Enter
replay only after recent imem backpressure makes this useful. A small
age counter records a stall while in live mode.

On entry pin the contiguous loop interval in the existing payload RAM
and pause live acceptance. Let any already queued older packets issue
through the existing RAM port. When the saved backedge issues, wrap
the read pointer to the saved head. If the backedge bypasses an empty
FIFO at entry, start at the head on the next cycle. After entry the
saved trace predicts fall-through for its interior and taken at its
backedge. The original packet PCs and full-width direct targets supply
resolution, and the saved gshare index trains the counter used to
capture that prediction. Pause the cursor for the ordinary
issue interlocks. Hold the external fetch request at the aligned loop
header while replay is active. A normal EX or late MEM miss, including
the loop exit, drops the pinned trace, squashes younger instructions,
and reopens the corrected live request with the existing empty bypass.
Prioritize the older MEM recovery. Keep last-word fetches live and
preserve full-width recovery, traps and RVFI ordering.

while any accepted FENCE.I is pending, accounting for advances and
squashes. Preserve the four-entry live capacity and the ready-bus
retirement schedule. On a ready-bus run the backpressure qualifier

in parallel with the admission decision. The replay mode bit locks

those flags and the legal displacement range at that boundary, so
the replay enable and retry path need a narrow test. During recovery

# In-place issue FIFO loop replay

The issue FIFO keeps four live entries in a 16-slot distributed RAM. Every accepted live response writes the ring, including an empty bypass. Capture requires an aligned, gshare-predicted conditional backedge with a target in the preceding 15 contiguous words. A live imem stall makes capture eligible for the next 15 cycles. The bitmap clears at discontinuities and can start a new run with a ready, sequential recovery response.

The prospective head and tail register in parallel with admission and freeze under replay mode. Older queued packets drain through the same read port before the cursor wraps at the saved tail. The RAM already contains the PC, full direct target, prediction and gshare index for each packet. The external request retries the loop header until an EX or older MEM recovery, when a ready corrected response can bypass the stale queue. FENCE.I acceptance clears capture history and the stall age. A count of accepted fences covers both queued and EX-held instructions and resets to the corrected path on recovery.

Each registered PC candidate carries a final-aperture-word flag. The hold uses the flag and the displacement range at that boundary. EX computes its flag in parallel with the recovery address. The final aperture word always fetches live. The top level exposes the single RVFI channel specified by `core.yaml`.

# Forward ADDI from the registered address sum

Issue registers two select bits per operand. The first gives an eligible EX/MEM writer priority over the older pair. The second selects the address or ALU result in the EX/MEM pair, or MEM/WB or the register-file snapshot in the older pair. Both producer comparisons exclude writes to x0, so x0 reads the register file's zero.

ID decodes the immediate and register forms of ADD separately. A fast ADDI forwards the registered full-width effective address and takes that same value through its one-hot MEM writeback lane. A true late ADDI dependency takes the existing MEM adder when the predecessor writes. When the predecessor traps, ADDI uses the ordinary address sum from the older operand. When a writing predecessor matches only encoded rs2, MEM updates the RVFI read value and ADDI still uses the registered address.

Register ADD receives forwarded rs2 directly. The other operations use the existing ALU operand selection. The ALU result merge groups the arithmetic terms and EX groups the link and AUIPC terms. # Reciprocal divider implementation

The bench divider now uses the nine-edge reciprocal schedule for DIV, DIVU, REM, and REMU. The existing phase counter still exposes readiness before the ninth edge, allows acceptance on that edge, and holds the final state when acceptance is deferred. The existing EX recovery reset cancels a squashed operation. ALTOPS captures its substitute result on the same final edge.

- The 512×34 synchronous ROM initializes from constant intercept and slope formulas. Interpolation registers the upper bits of `R*M - ((I << 22) + 1)` and complements them to recover the exact downward-rounded seed. This ordering lets Gowin infer a DSP multiply-subtract.
- The Newton and quotient stages retain full product widths before slicing. The quotient shift always discards bit 0 of the scaled quotient, so the masked product uses bits [32:1] and slices at bit 31. The registered mask lets that product start in parallel with the quotient shift.
- Edge nine computes the residual and precomputes the signed base result and corrected quotient. MEM uses a 33-bit residual subtraction for the correction decision and computes the remainder sign prefix in parallel. The result selection covers zero divisors and the 32-bit signed overflow case.

## Verification

- Verilator lint passed in normal and ALTOPS builds. All eight bench pytest runners passed, including fixed-latency signed and unsigned division, all 512 ROM intervals, normalization boundaries, exact multiples, deferred acceptance, reset at every divider phase, and dependent instructions after recovery. The ALTOPS runner checked the ninth-edge handoff for all four operations.
- `make cosim TARGET=bench NRET=1` passed the RVFI comparison with and without stalls and validated the stalled CoreMark CRCs. The explicit NRET matches the bench core's single-channel configuration. CoreMark completed ten iterations in 3,868,036 marker cycles.
- The stock `formal/run_all.sh` suite used the bench single-channel configuration. Liveness passed. The aggregate suite had 18 of 53 checks pass and no counterexamples before the time limit. Separate runs of the stock DIV, DIVU, REM, and REMU checks all passed.
- A bounded Yosys SAT comparison against the prior ALTOPS divider matched its handshake over 15 edges and its result with symbolic operands for immediate and deferred acceptance.

## Gowin

`make fpga TARGET=bench NRET=1` completed all three placements and validated stalled CoreMark.

| Placement option | Fmax |
| --- | ---: |
| 0 | 89.307 MHz |
| 1 | 88.462 MHz |
| 2 | 88.462 MHz |
| Median | 88.462 MHz |

The inferred design uses one pROMX9 for the coefficients, 12 DSP blocks in total, and 4,736 logic cells. The worst setup paths cross fetch recovery in option 0 and EX operand forwarding in options 1 and 2. The 88.462 MHz median falls below the 101.23 MHz promotion threshold and yields 228.70 iter/s.

A grouped-prefix variant used 4,288 logic cells and reached 88.071 MHz median. I kept the faster variant because CoreMark iterations per second determine promotion.

median, 22,876 net cycles saved would clear the 4.6% promotion threshold.

implementation_notes:
# Bench resident target replay

- Advancing, aligned, in-aperture taken conditional branches train a 64-entry admission bitmap for the source, target, and following target blocks. The older MEM branch has priority. Accepted ready responses stage fills for 512 exact-tag resident words.
- Fetch reads the ordinary held and sequential metadata banks every cycle. A parallel synchronous replica reads the saved direct target from the selected ordinary bank. Publication requires a valid source lookup, an accepted taken prediction, a matching full target and exact resident tag, and no lookup collision. A stalled request reserves its slot against a simultaneous fill at publication.
- The four-entry issue queue uses eight physical slots. Replay enqueues publish a resident slot, the applied gshare index and direction, and operand hints. Two speculative payload reads and a held-head register serve resident references. Fill logic pins the referenced slots through their pop edge. The wide live payload write uses the spare slot independently of replay publication.
- Reset and accepted FENCE.I scrub all metadata banks in 256 cycles. Pending fences block replay and fills. Older MEM recovery overrides EX recovery, and recovery rebases the queue at the corrected live request. A consecutive taken transfer from the target lane falls back to the ordinary request path for its successor.
- The live last-aperture-word behavior follows r10s1 so a legal predicted taken transfer there keeps its ready-bus schedule. The last word and unsupported replay transfers are excluded from resident fills.

## Local verification

- Strict Verilator lint and all seven cocotb runners passed. The directed tests cover ready-bus priority, replayed sources, exact-tag aliases, lookup-time fill collisions, FENCE.I, and a replay reference squashed by older MEM recovery into DIV with the 10-cycle retirement gap.
- Ready and stalled selftest ISS comparison passed. The ready selftest trace, including retirement cycles, matches r10s1 byte for byte. Ready CoreMark takes 3,064,374 marker cycles on both cores. Three additional stalled random ISS comparisons passed, and all 2,937,037 stalled CoreMark retirement records matched the Python ISS.
- Canonical CoreMark passed all five CRCs in both lane configurations. `BENCH_COUNT_TARGET_REPLAYS` enables the simulation-only marker counter. `ENABLE_TARGET_REPLAY` defaults to one and can be overridden for the comparison.

| Target lane | Accepted target replays within markers | CoreMark marker cycles |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Disabled | 0 | 3,397,267 |
| Enabled | 68,836 | 3,381,599 |

The target lane saved 15,668 marker cycles. The initial formal invocation stopped at Yosys parsing of a type-form `$bits` expression. Signal-form widths fixed elaboration. At the local time limit, 37 of 53 checks had passed with zero reported failures. The register check was still in the solver.

## Gowin timing

All placements routed. The three Fmax measurements were 80.137, 81.613, and 81.613 MHz. The median projects 241.34 CoreMark iterations/s. Promotion at the measured cycle count requires 88.496 MHz.

The worst setup paths run from MEM recovery into ID issue and instruction registers. Placement 0 also reports EX forwarding into the ALU among its worst paths. The target metadata read address and wide live FIFO write do not appear in the 25 worst setup paths in any placement report.
lesson: - 2026-11-22 hyp-20261122-003-r15s2 (regression, -3.54%): With a four-entry issue queue that can absorb fetch stalls, the synchronous taken-target metadata lane saved 15,668 stalled CoreMark marker cycles across 68,836 target replays, and MEM recovery paths into ID limited median Gowin Fmax to 81.613 MHz versus the 88.496 MHz needed for promotion.
